maria.p: Heads-up — after the kernel-affinity tweak deployed yesterday we're seeing a 7-12% p50 regression on small prefill batches for 7B models when decode load is >60% of the runner. Repro: qps=120, decode fraction ~0.65, prefill batches of 2-4 sequences. Logs + perf attached in thread.
jon: Hmm. Can you paste the perf counters and the kernel-selection trace? Curious if it's an extra memcpy or kernel fallback.
maria.p: Copied a small snippet from the profiler:
```
[run 12:54] model: redwood-7b; seq=256; prefill_batch=3
kernel_choice: fused_attn_fp16:cudnn_v2 -> exec_time=42.1ms
kernel_choice (decode): attn_causal_qkv_fp16:opt -> exec_time=12.5ms
cpu_fallbacks: 0
kv_hit_rate(prefill): 0.72
kv_hit_rate(decode): 0.89
p50_total(prefill): 58ms -> 65ms after deploy
```
No CPU fallbacks but prefill per-token exec time up ~10%. KV metrics look worse for prefill; suspect priming thrash when decode is saturating the KV priming window.
ops-bot: Deploy 2023-11-08T12:43:21 by infra/rolling-kernels. Rollout: 30% -> 100% (completed).
jon: If decode uses the lower-latency kernel aggressively it may be stealing preferred SM resources or changing stream scheduling. Also check whether prefill's selected kernel relies on a larger shared workspace that competes with decode.
tess: Quick idea: split token budget into phase-aware quotas so prefill has a reserved token budget slice. Right now we use a single token_budget_per_runner and let both prefill/decode race in the queue. Proposal:
- Introduce `phase_token_share` with default {prefill: 0.35, decode: 0.65} per runner.
- Enforce soft caps with hysteresis: if prefill waiting > 20ms and prefill_tokens < reserved -> bump prefill priority for next 50ms.
Implementation notes: rely on existing token-bucket but add `phase_bucket` and a short `hold_ms` to avoid flapping.
sam: I like reserving. We should also tune `batch_formation_window_ms` separately for phases — prefill can use a slightly longer formation window to accumulate sequences but we still bound tokens by `phase_token_share`.
alex: Watch out: kernel selector currently caches decisions keyed only by model+seq_len. If kernel behavior depends on concurrent phase mix (shared workspace pressure), selector cache becomes stale. We should add a cheap fingerprint including `phase_mix_bucket` when building the cache key.
maria.p: Good call. The profiler shows kernel_choice flip frequency jumped after deploy — cache misses up 18%.
jon: For a quick mitigation we can TTL the kernel cache shorter for 7B models (e.g., 1s -> 200ms) and add phase mix to the key as follow-up.
tess: Example config patch we could push to canary:
```
runtime.batch_policy:
  phase_split: true
  phase_token_share:
    prefill: 0.35
    decode: 0.65
  phase_hysteresis_ms: 50
  kernel_cache_ttl_ms: 200 # temporary for 7B canary
  batch_formation_window_ms:
    prefill: 8
    decode: 4
```
sam: Test plan:
1) Canary to 5% dedicated runners with the phase_split patch.
2) Run synthetic mixed-workload (qps/ratio sweep) and collect p50/p95 for prefill+decode, kv_hit_rate, kernel_cache_miss.
3) If >5% improvement in prefill p50 at same total throughput -> proceed to 30%.
4) Roll metrics: latency, tail, cost per token, GPU util, kernel_cache_miss.
alex: Also add a microbench for workspace contention: spin up two kernels (prefill kernel and decode kernel) concurrently on a test GPU and measure SM occupancy & memcpy overlap. This will tell us whether the collision is real or just scheduler noise.
maria.p: Results from a quick run (toy bench): when decode threads active, prefill kernel exec_time +14% and shared_mem_bandwidth skew increased. So it's not just cacheing; resource contention is real.
jon: OK. Actions:
- tess: open PR with `phase_split` config and default shares. (assign to tess)
- sam: set up canary harness + synthetic workload. (assign sam)
- alex: prototype kernel_cache key bump and add short TTL. (assign alex)
- maria.p: gather extended perf traces and KV warmup timelines for the A/B. (assign maria.p)
Everyone: post daily checkpoints in this thread. :thumbsup:
maria.p: Thanks — rolling the canary now for a small set of 7B runners. I'll post initial metrics in ~30m. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
